passages.text: Brijmohan Lall Munjal (1924-2015) founded Hero Cycles in 1956 and built it into the world's largest bicycle maker by volume, then extended the franchise into motorcycles through the 1984 joint venture with Honda, forming Hero Honda which became the world's largest two-wheeler manufacturer.

The 1984 Honda joint venture was the structural decision that defined the Hero story: by pairing Indian manufacturing and distribution reach with Japanese product technology, Munjal accessed the two-wheeler product curve without owning the technology stack, an arrangement that ran for 27 years before the amicable 2011 split.

The 2011 termination of the Honda JV and the rebrand to Hero MotoCorp tested whether the Indian partner could sustain product development without the Japanese counterparty, a transition whose outcome is now treated as evidence that the Indian distribution and brand could carry the franchise alone.

Munjal's operating discipline — capital intensity held low, dealer reach held high, model-platform cycles long — became the reference for how an Indian promoter house runs a volume consumer-durables business, and is the template the next generation of two-wheeler entrants measured themselves against.
